items: Version API responses with ETags, not hashed URLs
Endpoints are addressed by meaning, not by build
Purge is an out-of-band CDN call: fragile, eventually consistent
Busting is inherent and instant
Surrogate keys tag responses at the edge
Fastly and Cloudflare Enterprise expose tag purge
One call invalidates a whole content group

blocks.title: Service Worker Is Cache #4
items: You own it in JS, so you own its bugs
No `skipWaiting` / `clients.claim` = stale app forever
`curl -I` twice: `Age` climbs, `ETag` stays fixed
A CDN is a shared cache with PoPs near users
A hit avoids the origin RTT and the origin work
A miss pays both — hit ratio is the whole game
Headers: `x-cache`, `cf-cache-status`, `x-served-by`
Names differ per vendor, the states do not
Log the state, then slice latency by it
Origin shield: one mid-tier PoP fronts the origin
200 edge misses collapse into 1 origin fetch
Edge hit ratio and origin offload are different numbers
Track both — they diverge fast under tiering

lines: # both stripped before the client sees them

items: Order: `CDN-Cache-Control` > `Surrogate-Control` > `s-maxage` > `max-age`
Edge 1 day, browser 60s — no custom CDN rule needed
Well-behaved CDNs honour this precedence exactly

slides.page_title: CDN Behaviour and the Edge Layer

items: Most CDNs bypass cache when a response sets `Set-Cookie`
One stray cookie kills the hit rate, quietly
Many bypass when the request carries `Authorization`
Unless the response is explicitly marked `public`

blocks.title: Cache Key Hygiene
items: Strip `utm_*`, `fbclid`, `gclid` from the key
Else one page shards into a thousand entries
Lowercase host, sort params, fix trailing slashes

blocks.title: Cache poisoning
blocks.text: An unkeyed input like `X-Forwarded-Host` or `X-Original-URL` reflected into the body gets stored and served to everyone. Never reflect unkeyed headers; key on anything that changes the body.

items: ESI / edge fragments cache the shell, hole-punch personal parts
Measure hit ratio, origin offload %, bytes from edge
Report p50 and p99 split by cache state
A fresh hit costs zero
A 304 costs a full RTT plus ~200 bytes
That gap is the entire argument for `immutable`

left.title: Long TTL
items: High hit rate
Slow invalidation
Cheap origin
Scary mistakes

right.title: Short TTL
items: Fast propagation
Heavy origin load
Always near-fresh
Costly at scale
Pick per route, never once per site
Expiration is cheap and eventual
Invalidation is precise and operationally expensive
`no-store` — never written anywhere
`no-cache` — stored, always revalidated
`max-age=0` — stale at once, then normal stale rules
`private` still writes to the user's own disk

blocks.title: private is not no-store
blocks.text: `private` keeps the CDN out, not the shared laptop. Tokens and PII need `no-store`.

lines: # 5x the origin fleet for 40 points of hit rate

items: Hit ratio is not the goal — offload and p99 are
99% on tiny assets hides one hot uncached HTML route
Cache size is finite; LRU eviction is real
A huge long tail pushes your hot files out

blocks.title: Count your layers
blocks.text: Every caching layer is one more place truth can diverge. Add the next one only when you can name exactly what it fixes.

items: Caching authenticated HTML on a shared cache
User A sees user B's dashboard — use `private, no-store`
Assuming `no-cache` means do not cache
It means always revalidate; `no-store` is what you wanted
`max-age=31536000` on a non-fingerprinted URL
You pinned bad content on real browsers for a year
No recall path short of changing the URL
Forgetting `Vary: Accept-Encoding` — undecodable bodies
`Vary: User-Agent` or `Vary: Cookie` 'to be safe'
That disables shared caching and doubles origin load
`Set-Cookie` on a static asset — CDN silently refuses it
A 304 without refreshed `Cache-Control` / `ETag`
Entry stays stale, revalidates on every single request
Inode-derived ETags across a fleet, near-zero savings
Deleting old build artifacts on deploy — 404 chunks, white screen
Purging as a routine workflow instead of an emergency tool
Purge does not scale and is eventually consistent
Not caching 404s — a scanner becomes free origin load

blocks.title: Ctrl+Shift+R lies to you
blocks.text: A hard reload sends `Cache-Control: no-cache` and bypasses the exact behaviour you are testing. Use `curl` or a fresh profile instead.

blocks.title: The closing rule
blocks.text: Name the cache key, name the TTL, name the invalidation path. If you cannot state all three, you do not have a caching strategy.

Your app is probably fast for the wrong reason — and stale for a reason nobody wrote down. 10 pages on how HTTP caching actually works: freshness math, ETags vs Last-Modified, the conditional request dance, Vary as a hit-rate landmine, immutable assets, CDN precedence, and the mistakes that pin bad bytes on real browsers for a year.
